METHODOLOGY / COHERENCE REVIEW (round 2).

The IRIS optimization loop has two locked halves: MEASURE (a 3-layer eval, DL-0022) and EXPLORE (a candidate-generator that emits a ranked top-5 with confounder cards, DL-0023). This is the THIRD piece: M3 — the loop-driver that assembles the generator output into a morning report, gates it on human approval, routes approved items, and persists loop state across runs.

PROPOSAL:
IRIS optimization loop — M3 LOOP-DRIVER + MORNING REPORT + ROUTING + STATE, v1 (r2 consolidated). Measure=DL-0022; explore=DL-0023; top-5 cap=DL-0020; portable loop=DL-0021. Loop lives in dotdev; SUT is IRIS (classdojo/iris, separate repo). [tunable]=build constant; OPEN=human-input non-blocking.

A. LOOP STATE (single source of truth): committed JSON at loop/state.json on a dedicated `loop-state` branch in dotdev (NOT main — DL-0011 blocks direct main pushes; loop-state exempt from the main-protection ruleset). Tracks: baseline pointer {pinned IRIS commit, judge model, capture date, per-case pass map, P10 floor, permutation null}; per-case quarantine clocks; approved-not-yet-landed candidates; landed ledger {id, type, diff hash, approval ts, landed ts, merge SHA, human_edited:bool immutable}; change-counter since refresh; sentinel net time-series; suite version; fixture-gap queue pointer. Every run reads→appends→commits to loop-state. Each run validates a state schema + checksum and REFUSES to run on malformed/checksum-mismatched state; hand-edits go through `loop state edit` (schema-validate + rehash) or `loop state rehash`. v1: SINGLE-OPERATOR-AT-A-TIME + single-machine file lock (distributed lock deferred to auto mode).

B. RUN TRIGGER / IDEMPOTENCY: v1 manual `loop run`, keyed by {suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit-under-test + date}. Lifecycle: started → issue_posted:{url} → routed:{candidate_ids, pr_urls} → emitted. Re-run of the same key is idempotent; a crashed run (started, no emitted) RESUMES by checking what already succeeded (skip issue creation if issue_posted; skip a candidate's PR if its pr_url exists). Quarantine clocks advance ONLY on transition to emitted.

C. MORNING RANKED REPORT (read-only artifact, NOT the approval surface): markdown at loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md + posted as a dotdev issue (one per run, label loop-report). Sections: (1) HEADER — date, IRIS commit under test, baseline freshness + changes-since-baseline, judge model, suite version, counts (generated/passed-holdout/passed-FDR), budget used. (2) LOOP-HEALTH banner — sentinel net vs prior run (PASS/HALT), generator≠judge confirmation; on LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE emit ONLY the health section + zero candidates (health check strictly precedes candidate processing; no --force/--skip-health flag). (3) TOP-5 (net desc) — rank, net, type+blast tier, hypothesis, rendered diff, target cluster, full confounder card (cluster N, holdout N, permutation p, FDR q, cross-lane note, SOLE-DOMAIN + interpreted flags), proposed route target; HIGH-blast/cross-lane rendered as a distinct callout above the approval commands. (4) CANNOT-VALIDATE (separate, below the 5; human-judgment only). (5) FIXTURE-GAP queue status (count, oldest age, backlog-halt flag). (6) BLIND-SPOT lines — metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE count + examples; budget-exceeded clusters. (7) FOOTER — exact commands: loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>.

D. HUMAN APPROVAL GATE (CLI, per-candidate): `loop approve <date> <id>` writes {authenticated operator identity, ts, exact diff hash} to state; `loop reject <date> <id>` writes an explicit rejection; `loop edit <date> <id>` opens the diff in $EDITOR, on save validates + rehashes, writes {original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}, then REQUIRES a separate `loop approve` to finalize. DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed (no rubber-stamp by omission, no batch-approve, no --auto-approve flag in v1).

E. ROUTING (approved → target; one artifact per candidate, never batched; two-phase): write status=routing, routing_id=<id> to state BEFORE any PR/issue creation, write the artifact URL to state before advancing; on resume check if the artifact already exists before re-creating. Type 1 prompt/instruction → PR into classdojo/iris at the path from loop/config/iris-prompt-targets.yaml ({sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→paths), branch loop/<date>-<id>, body = hypothesis + confounder card + report link + [HUMAN-EDITED] if applicable. Type 2 reflection/habit → PR into classdojo/iris (v1 PR-only, no direct store write, so reconcile can always detect), scoped {scope, scope_key}. Type 3 tool schema/description → PR into iris. Type 4 retrieval-corpus → NOT auto-PR'd; human-judgment ISSUE in classdojo/iris (EVAL-INVISIBLE). Type 5 routing/findings-pipeline code → ISSUE into classdojo/iris (needs implementation), triage-labeled. Fixture-gap note → ISSUE in dotdev (fixture-audit label). Every artifact carries candidate id + report link + confounder card + [HUMAN-EDITED] marker, links back to the state ledger.

F. LANDED → LEDGER → BASELINE: `loop reconcile` runs automatically as the FIRST step of every `loop run`. It queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix loop/; per newly-merged PR: extract candidate id from the branch, verify merge SHA not already in the ledger (dedup guard), mark landed, increment change-counter. 'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch (the loop approve was the human-approval event; the GitHub merge is the landing event — no second approval). At change-counter=[5 tunable] OR a judge/IRIS model bump, the driver PROPOSES a baseline refresh (never auto); human confirms → capture run records a new baseline pointer AND resets quarantine clocks + re-quarantines the pre-refresh holdout set (DL-0023 §E).

G. PROVENANCE / MEASURING THE MEASURER: at each refresh, the DL-0023 §J delta-vs-last-baseline check attributes per-case regressions to the batch of ≤5 landed candidates since the last refresh (batch granularity, known limitation); human-edited candidates are INCLUDED in the batch with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag. A newly-regressed case raises CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION + surfaces the suspect batch in the next report for a human rollback decision (revert the suspect iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture baseline).

H. SECRETS / ACCESS: scoring needs warehouse creds + LLM keys (--execute --e2e). v1 uses operator local creds from env/secret store; keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs. A preflight in `loop run` verifies write access to classdojo/iris (branch + PR + issue) BEFORE scoring; failure aborts with a credential error. Secret-pattern scrubbing (sk-*, AKIA*, connection strings) on all LLM outputs before writing report/PR body. [OPEN: local vs CI runner].

I. AUTO MODE (deferred, M3 slice 6): v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path exists until a multi-run track record + trusted sentinel/health signal.

OPEN DECISIONS (human input, non-blocking): OD-1 iris prompt file paths (populate iris-prompt-targets.yaml); OD-2 habit/reflection store path in iris; OD-3 iris branch-protection effect on loop/ PRs; OD-4 local vs CI runner.

WORKED EXAMPLE: run 2026-08-01, IRIS@abc123, baseline fresh (2 changes since). Reconcile first (no new merges). Generator emits 3 validated; sentinel PASS. Top-3: #1 engagement-attribution habit (net 3, MEDIUM, [SOLE-DOMAIN]) → `loop approve 2026-08-01 1` → two-phase route → PR to iris at the habit path, branch loop/2026-08-01-1, body links report+card. #2 `loop edit 2026-08-01 2` (amend in $EDITOR) then `loop approve 2026-08-01 2` → routed [HUMAN-EDITED] (excluded from net-attribution, flagged in regression-attribution). #3 `loop reject 2026-08-01 3` or no action by deadline. A week later the PR merges → next run's reconcile marks landed, counter 2→3. At 5 the driver proposes a refresh; human confirms; capture resets quarantine per §E.

Round-1 blocking fixes to CONFIRM landed with no new blocker: (1) two-phase-commit crash recovery — run lifecycle started→issue_posted→routed{pr_urls}→emitted; resume skips already-created artifacts; quarantine clocks advance only at 'emitted'; (2) state on a dedicated `loop-state` branch (DL-0011 blocks main pushes); schema+checksum validated, refuses malformed state; (3) approval is CLI (`loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>`), GitHub issue is READ-ONLY; DEFAULT=REJECT enforced (no record by deadline = not routed); no --auto-approve flag; authenticated operator identity; (4) quarantine reset + re-quarantine at baseline refresh per DL-0023 §E; (5) Type-2 PR-only (no direct store write) so reconcile always detects; (6) reconcile auto-runs as FIRST step of every run, queries BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris for merged loop/ PRs, merge-SHA dedup; (7) [HUMAN-EDITED] marker immutable, excluded from net-attribution but INCLUDED (flagged) in regression-attribution; (8) iris-prompt-targets.yaml maps {sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→file paths; (9) single-operator-at-a-time v1 constraint + single-machine file lock; (10) preflight cross-repo write-access check aborts before scoring; (11) secret-pattern scrubbing on all LLM outputs before report/PR; (12) LOOP-HEALTH halt has no --force/--skip flag. ## Critique

**Summary:** The design is substantially coherent and round-1 fixes have all landed correctly; no new architectural blocker was introduced. Six residual issues remain — two require concrete resolution before implementation can be called idempotent or safe; the others are documentation/policy gaps resolvable in spec.

---

### Strong points

- **Two-phase commit structure** (write `status=routing` → create artifact → write URL → advance) is the correct pattern for crash-resumability; the sequence is internally consistent.
- **Quarantine-clock advancement at `emitted` only** correctly prevents partial-run double-advances; the run key `{suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit-under-test + date}` makes same-day re-runs converge to resume rather than re-execute.
- **DEFAULT=REJECT with no `--auto-approve`**, immutable `[HUMAN-EDITED]` flag, no batch-approve, and authenticated operator identity on `loop approve` are all correctly specified.
- **LOOP-HEALTH halt with no `--force`/`--skip` flag** is correctly enforced; health check strictly precedes candidate processing.
- **Type-2 PR-only** (no direct store write) preserves reconcile detectability.
- **Reconcile as FIRST step**, querying both repos, with merge-SHA dedup, is sound.
- **Cross-design coherence with DL-0022/DL-0023**: quarantine reset at refresh (§E), BH FDR over M_total (§F), sentinel design (§K), change-counter threshold (§J), and the holdout-first gate all cross-reference without contradiction.
- **Attribution honesty**: "batch ≤5, known limitation" is correctly disclosed as a real but weak signal, not handwaving.

---

### Weak points

#### 1. **Crash between artifact creation and URL write-back** — concrete mechanism unspecified [Q2, blocking]

The two-phase sequence is: `write status=routing` → `create PR/issue` → `write artifact URL` → advance. If the driver crashes after creating the PR/issue but before writing the artifact URL, resume finds `{status:routing, no artifact_url}` and the spec says "check if the artifact already exists before re-creating." But the mechanism is unspecified. For a GitHub PR, "already exists" means "a PR with branch `loop/<date>-<id>` is open against the target repo." Without specifying *how* this check is performed (e.g., `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo classdojo/iris --json url --state open`), the crash-resume idempotency guarantee is aspirational, not implemented. A branch push to an already-existing branch would fail at git-push time, not at PR-create time — so naive re-creation would leave a half-created state.

**Recommended fix:** Specify the resume probe: before creating any artifact, check for an open PR in the target repo with `head.ref == loop/<date>-<id>`; if found, extract its URL and write it to state, then continue without re-creating.

---

#### 2. **Approval deadline is undefined** [Q3, blocking]

§D says "no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed" and DEFAULT=REJECT is specified as a design invariant. But "routing deadline" is never defined. When does a candidate expire from `pending` to `rejected`? Options: 23:59 on the run date, start of the next `loop run`, a configurable TTL in `loop/config/`. Without a concrete definition, DEFAULT=REJECT has no triggering condition — candidates can linger as `pending` indefinitely, defeating the intent entirely.

**Recommended fix:** Lock the deadline semantics in spec: "a candidate is implicitly rejected when the *next* `loop run` completes reconcile (i.e., when a new report is emitted for the same or later date)." This is the lowest-friction choice for v1 and aligns with the daily-run cadence.

---

#### 3. **Candidate-ID dedup missing from the ledger** [Q1]

Reconcile deduplicates on merge SHA: "verify merge SHA not already in the ledger." But if a human error or race causes two loop/ PRs for the same candidate ID to both be merged (e.g., a stale worktree creates a second PR before seeing the first), reconcile would encounter two distinct merge SHAs and mark the candidate landed twice, incrementing the change-counter twice. The merge-SHA guard prevents re-processing one event but does not prevent double-landing.

**Recommended fix:** Add candidate-ID uniqueness as a secondary check: before marking a newly-reconciled candidate as landed, verify no existing ledger entry carries the same candidate ID. If a duplicate is found, surface a conflict warning rather than silently incrementing.

---

#### 4. **Reconcile's "branch prefix loop/" query does not filter by merge target** [Q4]

"Landed = merged to the target repo default branch" is the semantic definition, but "queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix `loop/`" is the implementation. GitHub's merged PR API returns PRs merged to *any* base branch. If a loop/ PR in iris is accidentally merged into a non-default branch (e.g., `staging`), reconcile would count it as landed and increment the change-counter — but the candidate change is not in iris's production code. This is a low-probability event, but "landed = merged to the target repo default branch" must be enforced in the query, not just stated as policy.

**Recommended fix:** Add `base:${defaultBranch}` to the reconcile GitHub query filter for classdojo/iris.

---

#### 5. **Approved-not-yet-landed PRs have no staleness path** [Q4]

An approved candidate routes to a PR in classdojo/iris. If that PR is closed without merge (reviewer rejects it, iris branch-protection blocks it per OD-3, or human abandons it), reconcile will never mark it landed. The `approved-not-yet-landed` ledger entry grows stale with no resolution path defined. Over multiple runs, this would cause state bloat and could mask genuine change-counter desync.

**Recommended fix:** Add a staleness alert in the morning report footer: "N candidates approved >30 days ago have not landed; review with `loop status`." Define `loop reject <date> <id>` as also valid for approved-but-stale to explicitly close them out.

---

#### 6. **CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION state machine is underspecified** [Q4]

§G says a newly-regressed case "surfaces the suspect batch in the next report for a human rollback decision." "Next report" (singular) implies it appears once. But if the human does not act, what happens in subsequent runs? Does it re-surface, escalate, or silently drop? A CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION with no persistence means a deferred human decision is equivalent to dismissal — which would be a safety gap. A CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION that re-surfaces every run is annoying but safe.

**Recommended fix:** Specify: CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persists as a banner in every subsequent report's LOOP-HEALTH section until a rollback is performed OR the human explicitly dismisses it via `loop dismiss-regression <date>` with a written rationale written to state. Dismissal is not the same as rollback — it's acknowledgment that the regression is acceptable or already tracked elsewhere.

---

#### 7. **CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates: approval mechanics unspecified** [Q3, minor]

CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates appear in a separate section and are "human-judgment only." But can a human issue `loop approve <date> <id>` for a CANNOT-VALIDATE candidate, bypassing statistical validation? If yes, the routing path must handle them (blast tier still applies, confounder card will be incomplete). If no, they are display-only. Neither is stated. Given DEFAULT=REJECT, the implicit answer is "they expire without action" — but if that's the intent, it should be stated explicitly so the CLI doesn't confuse "no approve command available" with "approval not yet given."

**Recommended fix:** State explicitly: CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates cannot be approved via `loop approve` in v1; they are informational only. Include a recommended action ("author a fixture if the case is real; otherwise use `loop reject`").

---

### Recommended correction (minimal)

The two blocking items (crash-resume probe mechanism, approval deadline definition) need to be resolved before implementation. The others can be resolved as spec amendments:

1. **Specify the crash-resume probe** for artifact existence (GitHub API branch/PR lookup by `head.ref`).
2. **Lock deadline semantics** ("next `loop run` reconcile completes" is the implicit-reject trigger).
3. Add candidate-ID dedup to ledger alongside merge-SHA dedup.
4. Add `base:${defaultBranch}` to reconcile query.
5. Define staleness alert + `loop reject` on approved-not-yet-landed.
6. Specify CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persistence until explicit dismissal or rollback.
7. State CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates are CLI-approve-ineligible in v1.

---

### Questions (blocking progress)

**Q-A:** What is the intended routing deadline for approvals — next-run-reconcile (implicit), fixed 24-hour TTL, or end-of-calendar-day? This must be chosen before implementing the `loop run` state-transition check. The design cannot enforce DEFAULT=REJECT without it.

**Q-B:** Is the crash-resume probe mechanism `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo classdojo/iris --json url --state open`, or something else? If the target repo (classdojo/iris) has API access constraints (OD-3 branch-protection impact), the probe must account for that. This is implementation-delegable but the *strategy* (GitHub API vs local branch-name registry in state.json) must be chosen now since it affects the crash-recovery contract.

**AGREE** — No bypass path exists.

- "DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed"

The fail-safe is correct: silence = rejection. An item can only route if an authenticated operator explicitly runs `loop approve <date> <id>`.

---

#### 2. STATE CORRUPTION
**AGREE** — Addressed for v1 constraints; git provides natural fail-safe.

Evidence from spec:
- "v1: SINGLE-OPERATOR-AT-A-TIME + single-machine file lock (distributed lock deferred to auto mode)"
- "Each run validates a state schema + checksum and REFUSES to run on malformed/checksum-mismatched state"

Crash recovery path: If crash occurs after PR creation but before URL written to state, resume queries GitHub for PRs matching branch `loop/<date>-<id>`. Branch name is deterministic → artifact is findable → no duplicate PR creation.

Concurrent access: If policy is violated (two operators on different machines), git push fails on the second operator since the branch tip moved. State corruption requires intentional bypass of both the policy AND the file lock.

---

#### 3. WRONG-TARGET / BLAST
**AGREE** — Target is human-approved; human-edited flag is policy-immutable.

- Report section C.3 shows "proposed route target" before approval

**Low hardening:** Error messages during auth failures could leak usernames or connection targets. Consider structured logging that omits connection details on failure.

---

#### 5. LOOP-HEALTH HALT
**AGREE** — Health failure halts candidate emission completely.

Evidence from spec:
- "on LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE emit ONLY the health section + zero candidates"
- "health check strictly precedes candidate processing"
- "no --force/--skip-health flag"

Control flow is unambiguous: health check runs before candidate processing; failure = zero candidates emitted. A subsequent `loop approve` for a *prior healthy run's* candidate is permitted — this is correct behavior (the candidate was generated when health was good, and the operator is making an explicit judgment call).

---

#### 6. AUTO-MODE
**AGREE** — No auto-approval path exists in v1.

Evidence from spec:
- "v1 fully human-gated"
- "no --auto-approve flag in v1"
- "DEFAULT=REJECT"
- "no batch-approve"

Every routing requires an explicit `loop approve` CLI call with authenticated identity. There is no timer, no quorum, no implicit approval mechanism.

---

### Round-1 Fixes Verification

| Fix | Status | Evidence |
|-----|--------|----------|
| Two-phase crash recovery | ✓ | lifecycle `started→issue_posted→routed→emitted`; resume checks artifact existence |
| State on `loop-state` branch | ✓ | "DL-0011 blocks direct main pushes; loop-state exempt" |
| CLI approval, issue READ-ONLY | ✓ | `loop approve/reject/edit`, DEFAULT=REJECT |
| Quarantine reset at refresh | ✓ | "per DL-0023 §E" |
| Type-2 PR-only | ✓ | "so reconcile can always detect" |
| Reconcile auto-runs FIRST | ✓ | "queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris" |
| HUMAN-EDITED immutable + flagged | ✓ | "immutable", "INCLUDED (flagged) in regression-attribution" |
| iris-prompt-targets.yaml | ✓ | maps types to paths |
| Single-operator + file lock | ✓ | "distributed lock deferred to auto mode" |
| Preflight cross-repo access | ✓ | "aborts before scoring" |
| Secret-pattern scrubbing | ✓ | all LLM outputs before report/PR |
| LOOP-HEALTH no --force | ✓ | explicitly prohibited |

---

### Medium Findings (defensive improvements)

**M1. `human_edited` immutability not enforced by `loop state edit`**
- The field is declared "immutable" but `loop state edit` has no stated validation rule preventing modification of existing ledger entries' `human_edited` flag
- Impact: Accidental (not malicious) corruption could let a human-edited candidate re-enter net-attribution
- Remediation: Add validation rule: `loop state edit` warns/blocks if `human_edited` changes for any existing ledger entry

**M2. Routing deadline undefined**
- The spec says "no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed" but never defines when this deadline is
- Impact: Clarity gap — does an unapproved candidate from 2026-08-01 eventually expire, or can it be approved months later?
- Remediation: Define: either (a) approval is valid until next baseline refresh, or (b) quarantine clock expiration also invalidates unapproved candidates from that run

---

### Low Findings (hardening suggestions)

**L1. Error logging may leak connection targets**
- Credential-error abort could log usernames, hostnames, or warehouse names
- Remediation: Structured logging that emits "preflight failed: {service}" without connection details

**L2. Checksum algorithm unspecified**
- "schema + checksum" validation mentions no algorithm
- Remediation: Specify (e.g., SHA-256 of canonicalized JSON) for implementation consistency

---

### Passes (sound aspects with evidence)

| Aspect | Evidence |
|--------|----------|
| No default-approve | "DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record... = NOT routed" |
| Crash recovery | Two-phase write + branch-name-deterministic artifact lookup |
| Concurrent access fail-safe | Git push fails if branch tip moved; schema+checksum rejects tampering |
| Health halt is unconditional | "no --force/--skip-health flag" |
| Human-edited tracking | "immutable" flag, included in regression attribution with [HUMAN-EDITED] marker |
| Cross-repo reconcile | "queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris" |

---

### Recommendation

**APPROVED** — Round-1 fixes are coherent and no new blocking design holes introduced.

The two medium findings are defensive hardening, not blockers. The design's fail-safes (DEFAULT=REJECT, git-backed state, explicit CLI approval, health halt without override) are correctly oriented.

---

### Decisions

1. **v1 concurrency model accepted:** Single-operator policy + file lock is sufficient for v1; git push conflict is an adequate fail-safe for accidental policy violation.
2. **Health halt scoping accepted:** Old candidates from healthy runs may be approved during a health-failed period — this is correct because the human operator is making an explicit judgment call with visibility into current health state.
3. **Pattern-based secret scrubbing accepted as defense-in-depth:** LLM inputs shouldn't contain secrets; scrubbing catches accidental exposure.
4. **Deferred to implementation:** Checksum algorithm, exact quarantine expiration semantics, `human_edited` edit-time validation rule.

PROPOSAL UNDER REVIEW:
IRIS optimization loop — M3 LOOP-DRIVER + MORNING REPORT + ROUTING + STATE, v1 (r2 consolidated). Measure=DL-0022; explore=DL-0023; top-5 cap=DL-0020; portable loop=DL-0021. Loop lives in dotdev; SUT is IRIS (classdojo/iris, separate repo). [tunable]=build constant; OPEN=human-input non-blocking.

PURPOSE: assemble the generator's ranked top-5 into a morning report, gate on genuine human approval, route approved items to real targets, persist loop state across runs. v1 manual; auto mode deferred.

A. LOOP STATE (single source of truth): committed JSON at loop/state.json on a dedicated `loop-state` branch in dotdev (NOT main — DL-0011 blocks direct main pushes; loop-state exempt from the main-protection ruleset). Tracks: baseline pointer {pinned IRIS commit, judge model, capture date, per-case pass map, P10 floor, permutation null}; per-case quarantine clocks; approved-not-yet-landed candidates; landed ledger {id, type, diff hash, approval ts, landed ts, merge SHA, human_edited:bool immutable}; change-counter since refresh; sentinel net time-series; suite version; fixture-gap queue pointer. Every run reads→appends→commits to loop-state. Each run validates a state schema + checksum and REFUSES to run on malformed/checksum-mismatched state; hand-edits go through `loop state edit` (schema-validate + rehash) or `loop state rehash`. v1: SINGLE-OPERATOR-AT-A-TIME + single-machine file lock (distributed lock deferred to auto mode).

B. RUN TRIGGER / IDEMPOTENCY: v1 manual `loop run`, keyed by {suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit-under-test + date}. Lifecycle: started → issue_posted:{url} → routed:{candidate_ids, pr_urls} → emitted. Re-run of the same key is idempotent; a crashed run (started, no emitted) RESUMES by checking what already succeeded (skip issue creation if issue_posted; skip a candidate's PR if its pr_url exists). Quarantine clocks advance ONLY on transition to emitted.

C. MORNING RANKED REPORT (read-only artifact, NOT the approval surface): markdown at loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md + posted as a dotdev issue (one per run, label loop-report). Sections: (1) HEADER — date, IRIS commit under test, baseline freshness + changes-since-baseline, judge model, suite version, counts (generated/passed-holdout/passed-FDR), budget used. (2) LOOP-HEALTH banner — sentinel net vs prior run (PASS/HALT), generator≠judge confirmation; on LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE emit ONLY the health section + zero candidates (health check strictly precedes candidate processing; no --force/--skip-health flag). (3) TOP-5 (net desc) — rank, net, type+blast tier, hypothesis, rendered diff, target cluster, full confounder card (cluster N, holdout N, permutation p, FDR q, cross-lane note, SOLE-DOMAIN + interpreted flags), proposed route target; HIGH-blast/cross-lane rendered as a distinct callout above the approval commands. (4) CANNOT-VALIDATE (separate, below the 5; human-judgment only). (5) FIXTURE-GAP queue status (count, oldest age, backlog-halt flag). (6) BLIND-SPOT lines — metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE count + examples; budget-exceeded clusters. (7) FOOTER — exact commands: loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>.

D. HUMAN APPROVAL GATE (CLI, per-candidate): `loop approve <date> <id>` writes {authenticated operator identity, ts, exact diff hash} to state; `loop reject <date> <id>` writes an explicit rejection; `loop edit <date> <id>` opens the diff in $EDITOR, on save validates + rehashes, writes {original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}, then REQUIRES a separate `loop approve` to finalize. DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed (no rubber-stamp by omission, no batch-approve, no --auto-approve flag in v1).

E. ROUTING (approved → target; one artifact per candidate, never batched; two-phase): write status=routing, routing_id=<id> to state BEFORE any PR/issue creation, write the artifact URL to state before advancing; on resume check if the artifact already exists before re-creating. Type 1 prompt/instruction → PR into classdojo/iris at the path from loop/config/iris-prompt-targets.yaml ({sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→paths), branch loop/<date>-<id>, body = hypothesis + confounder card + report link + [HUMAN-EDITED] if applicable. Type 2 reflection/habit → PR into classdojo/iris (v1 PR-only, no direct store write, so reconcile can always detect), scoped {scope, scope_key}. Type 3 tool schema/description → PR into iris. Type 4 retrieval-corpus → NOT auto-PR'd; human-judgment ISSUE in classdojo/iris (EVAL-INVISIBLE). Type 5 routing/findings-pipeline code → ISSUE into classdojo/iris (needs implementation), triage-labeled. Fixture-gap note → ISSUE in dotdev (fixture-audit label). Every artifact carries candidate id + report link + confounder card + [HUMAN-EDITED] marker, links back to the state ledger.

F. LANDED → LEDGER → BASELINE: `loop reconcile` runs automatically as the FIRST step of every `loop run`. It queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix loop/; per newly-merged PR: extract candidate id from the branch, verify merge SHA not already in the ledger (dedup guard), mark landed, increment change-counter. 'landed' = merged to the target repo default branch (the loop approve was the human-approval event; the GitHub merge is the landing event — no second approval). At change-counter=[5 tunable] OR a judge/IRIS model bump, the driver PROPOSES a baseline refresh (never auto); human confirms → capture run records a new baseline pointer AND resets quarantine clocks + re-quarantines the pre-refresh holdout set (DL-0023 §E).

G. PROVENANCE / MEASURING THE MEASURER: at each refresh, the DL-0023 §J delta-vs-last-baseline check attributes per-case regressions to the batch of ≤5 landed candidates since the last refresh (batch granularity, known limitation); human-edited candidates are INCLUDED in the batch with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag. A newly-regressed case raises CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION + surfaces the suspect batch in the next report for a human rollback decision (revert the suspect iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture baseline).

H. SECRETS / ACCESS: scoring needs warehouse creds + LLM keys (--execute --e2e). v1 uses operator local creds from env/secret store; keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs. A preflight in `loop run` verifies write access to classdojo/iris (branch + PR + issue) BEFORE scoring; failure aborts with a credential error. Secret-pattern scrubbing (sk-*, AKIA*, connection strings) on all LLM outputs before writing report/PR body. [OPEN: local vs CI runner].

I. AUTO MODE (deferred, M3 slice 6): v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path exists until a multi-run track record + trusted sentinel/health signal.

OPEN DECISIONS (human input, non-blocking): OD-1 iris prompt file paths (populate iris-prompt-targets.yaml); OD-2 habit/reflection store path in iris; OD-3 iris branch-protection effect on loop/ PRs; OD-4 local vs CI runner.

WORKED EXAMPLE: run 2026-08-01, IRIS@abc123, baseline fresh (2 changes since). Reconcile first (no new merges). Generator emits 3 validated; sentinel PASS. Top-3: #1 engagement-attribution habit (net 3, MEDIUM, [SOLE-DOMAIN]) → `loop approve 2026-08-01 1` → two-phase route → PR to iris at the habit path, branch loop/2026-08-01-1, body links report+card. #2 `loop edit 2026-08-01 2` (amend in $EDITOR) then `loop approve 2026-08-01 2` → routed [HUMAN-EDITED] (excluded from net-attribution, flagged in regression-attribution). #3 `loop reject 2026-08-01 3` or no action by deadline. A week later the PR merges → next run's reconcile marks landed, counter 2→3. At 5 the driver proposes a refresh; human confirms; capture resets quarantine per §E.

SPECIALIST REVIEWS:
### [1/3] critic

## Critique

**Summary:** The design is substantially coherent and round-1 fixes have all landed correctly; no new architectural blocker was introduced. Six residual issues remain — two require concrete resolution before implementation can be called idempotent or safe; the others are documentation/policy gaps resolvable in spec.

---

### Strong points

- **Two-phase commit structure** (write `status=routing` → create artifact → write URL → advance) is the correct pattern for crash-resumability; the sequence is internally consistent.
- **Quarantine-clock advancement at `emitted` only** correctly prevents partial-run double-advances; the run key `{suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit-under-test + date}` makes same-day re-runs converge to resume rather than re-execute.
- **DEFAULT=REJECT with no `--auto-approve`**, immutable `[HUMAN-EDITED]` flag, no batch-approve, and authenticated operator identity on `loop approve` are all correctly specified.
- **LOOP-HEALTH halt with no `--force`/`--skip` flag** is correctly enforced; health check strictly precedes candidate processing.
- **Type-2 PR-only** (no direct store write) preserves reconcile detectability.
- **Reconcile as FIRST step**, querying both repos, with merge-SHA dedup, is sound.
- **Cross-design coherence with DL-0022/DL-0023**: quarantine reset at refresh (§E), BH FDR over M_total (§F), sentinel design (§K), change-counter threshold (§J), and the holdout-first gate all cross-reference without contradiction.
- **Attribution honesty**: "batch ≤5, known limitation" is correctly disclosed as a real but weak signal, not handwaving.

---

### Weak points

#### 1. **Crash between artifact creation and URL write-back** — concrete mechanism unspecified [Q2, blocking]

The two-phase sequence is: `write status=routing` → `create PR/issue` → `write artifact URL` → advance. If the driver crashes after creating the PR/issue but before writing the artifact URL, resume finds `{status:routing, no artifact_url}` and the spec says "check if the artifact already exists before re-creating." But the mechanism is unspecified. For a GitHub PR, "already exists" means "a PR with branch `loop/<date>-<id>` is open against the target repo." Without specifying *how* this check is performed (e.g., `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo classdojo/iris --json url --state open`), the crash-resume idempotency guarantee is aspirational, not implemented. A branch push to an already-existing branch would fail at git-push time, not at PR-create time — so naive re-creation would leave a half-created state.

**Recommended fix:** Specify the resume probe: before creating any artifact, check for an open PR in the target repo with `head.ref == loop/<date>-<id>`; if found, extract its URL and write it to state, then continue without re-creating.

---

#### 2. **Approval deadline is undefined** [Q3, blocking]

§D says "no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed" and DEFAULT=REJECT is specified as a design invariant. But "routing deadline" is never defined. When does a candidate expire from `pending` to `rejected`? Options: 23:59 on the run date, start of the next `loop run`, a configurable TTL in `loop/config/`. Without a concrete definition, DEFAULT=REJECT has no triggering condition — candidates can linger as `pending` indefinitely, defeating the intent entirely.

**Recommended fix:** Lock the deadline semantics in spec: "a candidate is implicitly rejected when the *next* `loop run` completes reconcile (i.e., when a new report is emitted for the same or later date)." This is the lowest-friction choice for v1 and aligns with the daily-run cadence.

---

#### 3. **Candidate-ID dedup missing from the ledger** [Q1]

Reconcile deduplicates on merge SHA: "verify merge SHA not already in the ledger." But if a human error or race causes two loop/ PRs for the same candidate ID to both be merged (e.g., a stale worktree creates a second PR before seeing the first), reconcile would encounter two distinct merge SHAs and mark the candidate landed twice, incrementing the change-counter twice. The merge-SHA guard prevents re-processing one event but does not prevent double-landing.

**Recommended fix:** Add candidate-ID uniqueness as a secondary check: before marking a newly-reconciled candidate as landed, verify no existing ledger entry carries the same candidate ID. If a duplicate is found, surface a conflict warning rather than silently incrementing.

---

#### 4. **Reconcile's "branch prefix loop/" query does not filter by merge target** [Q4]

"Landed = merged to the target repo default branch" is the semantic definition, but "queries merged PRs in BOTH dotdev + classdojo/iris with branch prefix `loop/`" is the implementation. GitHub's merged PR API returns PRs merged to *any* base branch. If a loop/ PR in iris is accidentally merged into a non-default branch (e.g., `staging`), reconcile would count it as landed and increment the change-counter — but the candidate change is not in iris's production code. This is a low-probability event, but "landed = merged to the target repo default branch" must be enforced in the query, not just stated as policy.

**Recommended fix:** Add `base:${defaultBranch}` to the reconcile GitHub query filter for classdojo/iris.

---

#### 5. **Approved-not-yet-landed PRs have no staleness path** [Q4]

An approved candidate routes to a PR in classdojo/iris. If that PR is closed without merge (reviewer rejects it, iris branch-protection blocks it per OD-3, or human abandons it), reconcile will never mark it landed. The `approved-not-yet-landed` ledger entry grows stale with no resolution path defined. Over multiple runs, this would cause state bloat and could mask genuine change-counter desync.

**Recommended fix:** Add a staleness alert in the morning report footer: "N candidates approved >30 days ago have not landed; review with `loop status`." Define `loop reject <date> <id>` as also valid for approved-but-stale to explicitly close them out.

---

#### 6. **CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION state machine is underspecified** [Q4]

§G says a newly-regressed case "surfaces the suspect batch in the next report for a human rollback decision." "Next report" (singular) implies it appears once. But if the human does not act, what happens in subsequent runs? Does it re-surface, escalate, or silently drop? A CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION with no persistence means a deferred human decision is equivalent to dismissal — which would be a safety gap. A CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION that re-surfaces every run is annoying but safe.

**Recommended fix:** Specify: CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persists as a banner in every subsequent report's LOOP-HEALTH section until a rollback is performed OR the human explicitly dismisses it via `loop dismiss-regression <date>` with a written rationale written to state. Dismissal is not the same as rollback — it's acknowledgment that the regression is acceptable or already tracked elsewhere.

---

#### 7. **CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates: approval mechanics unspecified** [Q3, minor]

CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates appear in a separate section and are "human-judgment only." But can a human issue `loop approve <date> <id>` for a CANNOT-VALIDATE candidate, bypassing statistical validation? If yes, the routing path must handle them (blast tier still applies, confounder card will be incomplete). If no, they are display-only. Neither is stated. Given DEFAULT=REJECT, the implicit answer is "they expire without action" — but if that's the intent, it should be stated explicitly so the CLI doesn't confuse "no approve command available" with "approval not yet given."

**Recommended fix:** State explicitly: CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates cannot be approved via `loop approve` in v1; they are informational only. Include a recommended action ("author a fixture if the case is real; otherwise use `loop reject`").

---

### Recommended correction (minimal)

The two blocking items (crash-resume probe mechanism, approval deadline definition) need to be resolved before implementation. The others can be resolved as spec amendments:

1. **Specify the crash-resume probe** for artifact existence (GitHub API branch/PR lookup by `head.ref`).
2. **Lock deadline semantics** ("next `loop run` reconcile completes" is the implicit-reject trigger).
3. Add candidate-ID dedup to ledger alongside merge-SHA dedup.
4. Add `base:${defaultBranch}` to reconcile query.
5. Define staleness alert + `loop reject` on approved-not-yet-landed.
6. Specify CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persistence until explicit dismissal or rollback.
7. State CANNOT-VALIDATE candidates are CLI-approve-ineligible in v1.

---

### Questions (blocking progress)

**Q-A:** What is the intended routing deadline for approvals — next-run-reconcile (implicit), fixed 24-hour TTL, or end-of-calendar-day? This must be chosen before implementing the `loop run` state-transition check. The design cannot enforce DEFAULT=REJECT without it.

**Q-B:** Is the crash-resume probe mechanism `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo classdojo/iris --json url --state open`, or something else? If the target repo (classdojo/iris) has API access constraints (OD-3 branch-protection impact), the probe must account for that. This is implementation-delegable but the *strategy* (GitHub API vs local branch-name registry in state.json) must be chosen now since it affects the crash-recovery contract.

---

### [2/3] analyst

## Analysis

### Known (confirmed by design doc + repo context)

- DL-0021–0023 locked. Candidate types, blast tiers, scoring, confounder card, and holdout guard are fully specified.
- Fixtures (`golden_sql` 25 pairs, `expected_answer_facts`) live in **classdojo/iris** (`backend/src/iris/eval/`), confirmed by DL-0021 and P0a tracking under iris issue lineage (IRIS #945 ancestor).
- OD-1 (iris prompt file paths) and OD-2 (habit/reflection store path) are explicitly open, marked non-blocking for design but **fully blocking for Type 1 and Type 2 routing at runtime**.
- DL-0011 confirms `main-protection` ruleset is active on dotdev; `loop-state` branch is designed to be exempt. That exemption is asserted in the design but no evidence it was encoded in the ruleset (the DL shows the ruleset was created via API with no bypass actors named).

---

### Review by Element

---

#### Element 1 — Route targets map to real IRIS surfaces

**Type 1 (prompt/instruction) → AGREE in structure, OBJECT on two gaps**

The yaml-bridged routing to `{sql_generation, findings_prose, system_prefix}` is sound. Two gaps:

- **Gap 1a — No path-existence validation before PR creation.** The preflight checks write-access to iris but not whether the target path in `iris-prompt-targets.yaml` exists in the current iris HEAD. If iris refactors prompt file locations after the yaml is populated (OD-1), the two-phase commit writes `status=routing`, attempts to create a branch, pushes a diff to a nonexistent file, and leaves state stranded in `routing`. The crash-resume logic then re-attempts the same bad path forever. **Fix:** add a `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<path>?ref=<iris-commit>` existence check per route target, immediately before creating the PR branch; abort with a `ROUTE-TARGET-STALE` error and write that to state rather than entering the two-phase commit.

- **Gap 1b — Type 3 (tool schema/description) has no target-path mechanism.** DL-0023 §A specifies Type 1 carries `{target_prompt}` and Type 2 carries `{scope, scope_key}`. Type 3 carries nothing. Section E of the loop driver says "PR into iris" for Type 3 but gives no path resolution mechanism — no equivalent yaml, no field in the candidate struct. At routing time the driver cannot know which file to patch. **Fix:** require Type 3 candidates to carry a `{target_tool_path}` field (analogous to Type 1's `target_prompt`), and add a `loop/config/iris-tool-targets.yaml` or inline path annotation before build.

**Type 2 (reflection/habit) → OBJECT**

The "PR-only, no direct store write" constraint is correct for reconcile detectability. But OD-2 is not merely a path *name* — it's the entire question of whether a Type 2 candidate has an addressable file in iris at all. `{scope, scope_key}` is metadata, not a file path. Until OD-2 resolves to a concrete path, a Type 2 PR has no `diff` with a valid `+++` line; the PR body would contain the hypothesis and confounder card but no actual file change. This is worse than OD-1 (which has a placeholder yaml) — Type 2 has no placeholder at all. **Fix:** require OD-2 to produce a `loop/config/iris-habit-targets.yaml` (or equivalent path resolver) before Type 2 routing is enabled in the driver; at build time, Type 2 routing should fail-fast with `ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2` rather than emitting an empty-diff PR.

**Type 4 (retrieval-corpus) → AGREE**

EVAL-INVISIBLE, human-judgment issue in iris, not auto-PR'd. This is correct and consistent with DL-0022 §A.4's acknowledged v1 structural blind spot.

**Type 5 (routing/findings-pipeline code) → AGREE**

Issue into iris, triage-labeled, not auto-PR'd. Correct: code changes need a human implementer.

**Fixture-gap note → OBJECT (wrong repo)**

The design routes fixture-gap notes to **dotdev issues** (`fixture-audit` label). But the golden fixtures — `expected_answer_facts`, the 25 `golden_sql` pairs — live in **classdojo/iris** (`backend/src/iris/eval/`). P0a work (which is exactly fixture-gap remediation) has been tracked as an iris-repo concern. Routing fixture-gap notes to dotdev splits tracking: the loop operator sees the gap report in dotdev while the iris maintainers who own the fixture files see nothing until someone manually transfers the issue. **Fix:** fixture-gap notes → ISSUE in **classdojo/iris** (not dotdev), with a `fixture-audit` label and a link back to the dotdev report. The dotdev report can carry the count as a section C(5) status line; ownership follows the artifact.

---

#### Element 2 — Cross-repo routing actually works and lands in the right place

**AGREE on architecture; one concrete gap.**

The `gh` CLI two-phase commit, preflight write-access check, reconcile querying both repos for `loop/`-prefixed branches, and artifact-URL tracking in state form a coherent cross-repo execution model.

**Gap — Dedup key is SHA-only, not (repo, merge_sha).** The reconcile step says: "verify merge SHA not already in the ledger (dedup guard)." Merge SHAs are namespaced per repo. If the ledger stores only the SHA string, two distinct candidates landed in two different repos could theoretically collide (astronomically unlikely but structurally imprecise), and more importantly the ledger has no way to reconstruct *which repo* a SHA belongs to for audit purposes. **Fix:** the ledger entry for `merge_sha` should be stored as `{repo: "classdojo/iris" | "dotdev", sha: "<sha>"}` and the dedup check should match on both fields.

**OD-3 (iris branch protection on loop/ PRs) is flagged as non-blocking but has a concrete operational consequence:** if iris requires CI to pass before merge, an approved loop/ PR can be blocked indefinitely by a failing test the loop didn't author. The state machine has no `ci-failing` transition — it stays in `approved-not-yet-landed` with no operator guidance. This doesn't block design but needs a runbook entry (see Element 4).

---

#### Element 3 — Report surfaces IRIS-specific risk where operator sees it before approving

**AGREE on structure; two gaps.**

The report design is strong: HIGH-blast/cross-lane callout *above* approval commands (not below), full confounder card with cross-lane note and SOLE-DOMAIN flag, BLIND-SPOT section for metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE, and CANNOT-VALIDATE separate from the top-5. An operator reading top-to-bottom will hit the risk context before the approval command.

**Gap 3a — "Proposed route target" is incomplete for Types 1/2 until OD-1/OD-2 resolve.** Section C(3) lists "proposed route target" as a top-5 field. If OD-1 is unpopulated, a Type 1 entry shows `sql_generation` without a file path. The operator cannot assess blast radius — "sql_generation prompt edit" tells them the logical target but not which file in iris is being patched or how many call sites reference it. Until OD-1/OD-2 resolve, the report should render either the fully-resolved path or a prominent `[ROUTE-UNRESOLVED: OD-1 pending — approval will be recorded but routing will fail]` warning inline, not a silent placeholder. This is an actionability failure specifically for the IRIS operator who needs the concrete file path to judge risk.

**Gap 3b — Routing deadline is never defined.** Section D says: "no approval record by the routing deadline = NOT routed." The footer (Section C(7)) shows the approval commands but states no deadline. The routing deadline does not appear anywhere in the design. If the operator reads Friday's report and returns Monday, are approvals still valid? Is the deadline "before the next `loop run`"? "24 hours"? "7 days"?
